headline: AI capex scrutiny hits mega-caps while broader market holds up
body: This week's megacap earnings have turned into a referendum on AI spending rather than growth. Alphabet fell roughly 12% on Thursday, its worst one-day move in years, despite cloud revenue growth accelerating past 100%, as investors zeroed in on compressed free cash flow and lingering doubts about near-term AI returns. Amazon followed the same script after Wednesday's close: a solid AWS beat, with revenue up about 39% year-over-year, was overshadowed by a roughly $220 billion 2026 capex plan and a slightly light fourth-quarter revenue outlook, sending the stock down more than 10% between the regular session and after-hours trading. The pattern across both reports is consistent: strong underlying demand on its own is no longer enough, and the market now wants a visible path from spending to profit before it rewards the stock.

The damage looks more like a rotation than a broad flight from risk. The Nasdaq absorbed the brunt of Thursday's selling, down about 1.7%, while the small-cap Russell 2000 advanced and chip stocks, after a four-session winning streak, pulled back only modestly as traders sorted names that can self-fund their AI buildouts from those leaning harder on outside capital. That split sits alongside a Federal Reserve that held rates steady this week in a closely watched, non-unanimous vote, with only a muted market reaction either way. Retail-sentiment chatter on the AI-capex names is thin relative to the size of the price moves, so today's read leans on earnings reactions and index behavior rather than social-media positioning; the overall mood looks like selective caution concentrated in a handful of mega-caps, not broad-based pessimism.
